newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures surfed a wave of positive sentiment in European bond markets to reach their highest level this year amid fading concerns about potentially negative German data due this week.

Traders said Monday's rally was not particularly solid, as volume was low, but in the absence of any surprises there was no reason why the contract could not set its sights on a target of 128.50, with the gap to 128.10 the next hurdle.
The December contract hit an intra-day high of 127.96 before profit taking, notably from one fund at the highs, sent it lower to settle at 127.86.
"The French market is following the German market and there's no more than that," Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley in Paris, said.

Chaney said fears about a strong rise in German M3 this week had been debunked by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing and the Ifo business sentiment survey, due on Wednesday, could be seen as positive whether it were to come in strong or weak.

"A good Ifo survey means recovery in the mark zone, including France, is still on track, which makes the stability pact negotiations easier," Chaney said. "If it's bad, the markets will speculate about an cut in German rates."
Issing said on Friday German investment in new Deutsche Telekom shares could boost M3 in the short term.
Traders said the Matif rally had been led by local traders who managed to trigger stops on the way to the previous contract high of 127.80.
One trader said taking away the volume from local traders and that involved in spread trades between the December and March bond contracts the session had not been that active.
Chaney said his end of year target for the 10-year bond yield of 5.80 percent had already been reached and he would not rule out seeing the bond future at 130 by the end of December.
The yield on the 6.50 percent October 2006 OAT was at 5.80 percent late on Monday, down from 5.83 on Friday. The spread over 10-year Bunds moved back to parity from two basis points on Friday.
Analysts said there was little concern about two- and five-year government supply due this week. Both spreads narrowed two basis points compared with their German counterparts.
The Treasury will give the amount of the 4.50 percent 1998 and 5.50 percent 2001 BTANs on offer at Thursday's regular auction from 1000 GMT on Tuesday.

The fact call money remained unchanged on Monday failed to dampen expectations for a cut in the French overnight rate and December PIBOR posted a contract high at 96.50 percent. The interest rate future lagged three month cash which was trading at 3.39 percent.
Analysts said they were eyeing the outcome of the French parliament debate on pension funds on Thursday to gauge the implications for allocation of assets between stocks and bonds.
